subject: Post-call: Peregrine discovery + recommended pilot models & verified perf
messages:
From: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>
To: Lauren Cole <lauren@peregrinelabs.com>, Chris Nguyen <chris@peregrinelabs.com>
Cc: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 30 Sep 2026 15:12:00 -0700
Subject: Post-call: Peregrine discovery + recommended pilot models & verified perf

Hi Lauren / Chris — great to meet you both earlier. Quick recap and clear next steps so we can get a pilot scoped.

Call highlights:
- Primary goal: productionize semantic search + contextual Q&A for internal docs (avg doc length ~800 tokens).
- SLA target: p95 latency <= 200ms for single-query lookups; batch index/ingest throughput matters less for now.
- Expected concurrency: 40 interactive users with occasional bursts to 250 sessions.
- Data sensitivity: internal engineering docs (no PHI), they'd prefer Private deployment but open to Dedicated for POC.

Recommended pilot slate (shortlist we discussed):
1) redwood/llama-3-8b-q4 (quantized) — best latency/cost tradeoff for short queries.
2) mix-13b-8k-finetuned — higher quality on contextual Q&A; more memory but better F1 on our prompt sets.
3) davinci-like-compat-7b (opt) — fallback for low-cost bulk rerank jobs.

I attached a short "Peregrine benchmark summary" with Redwood-verified profiles and the prompt_set_search_v1.json we used to generate the perf runs. The linked Drive folder has raw traces and p99 traces. Key perf snippets (from Redwood-verified profiles):
- llama-3-8b-q4 (batch=8, seq=512): throughput ~420 tokens/sec, p50=38ms, p90=95ms, p99=240ms.
- mix-13b-8k (batch=4, seq=1024): throughput ~210 tokens/sec, p50=72ms, p90=155ms, p99=400ms.
- davinci-7b-compat (batch=16, seq=256): throughput ~620 tokens/sec, p50=30ms, p90=70ms, p99=180ms.

Suggested pilot configuration:
- Two-week functional validation: run search and Q&A prompts from prompt_set_search_v1 against 10k doc corpus.
- Perf validation: narrowed load test to 40 sustained users with a 250-user burst window. We'll measure p50/p90/p99 and stabilise batching.
- Quality check: run 200 curated queries for regression detection (we'll attach a baseline MRR/EM table).

Next steps (action owners):
- Ben: share pilot SOW + HubSpot deal (done) and DocuSign for PO when ready.
- Marissa: share detailed perf profiles and recommended node sizing for Dedicated/Private.
- Stephanie: open procurement thread and provide SOC 2 / security checklist responses.

If this looks right I'll queue the benchmark folder and the Redwood-verified perf TSV for your engineering team. Happy to set a follow-up with DevOps next week.

Thanks,
Ben Carter
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
ben@redwood.com | +1 415-555-0123

Cc: Lauren Cole <lauren@peregrinelabs.com>

Subject: Re: Post-call: Peregrine discovery + recommended pilot models & verified perf

Ben / Steph — adding the deeper perf & pilot guidance (pulling from the Redwood-verified runs). Answering Lauren's questions inline: 

1) Latency scope: the numbers I shared are model-inference-only (server-side token generation). End-to-end p95 will depend on your retrieval latency + network hop. For planning, assume an additional 40–80ms for a single retrieval roundtrip and 20–40ms for network egress (varies by region). That means the llama-3-8b-q4 config should comfortably meet ~p95 <= 200–220ms for simple retrieval+inference flows in the us-east region with colocated embedding store.

2) Fallback/runbooks: we recommend the following policy (we can ship this as part of the pilot):
- Primary: redwood/llama-3-8b-q4 (low-latency).
- Secondary: davinci-7b-compat for high-throughput rerank/short queries (cheaper, faster at small seq).
- Auto-scale: Dedicated pool with burst capacity to handle 2x normal concurrent load (warm pool).
- Graceful degrade: if p90>350ms, automatically route to the secondary model with a request-level signal and add a quality guardrail to mark answers as "possibly degraded" in logs.

Pilot node sizing (recommended Dedicated small pool):
- 3 x a100-40GB-equivalent GPUs (2 for inference, 1 as warm standby/burst).
- Estimated POC cost: $12k–$18k/mo depending on usage and data egress (we'll provide a more precise breakdown in the SOW).

Redwood-verified perf profile highlights (full TSV attached):
- redwood/llama-3-8b-q4 (seq=512, batch=8): 420 tok/s, p50=38ms, p90=95ms, p99=240ms.
- mix-13b-8k-finetuned (seq=1024, batch=4): 210 tok/s, p50=72ms, p90=155ms, p99=400ms.
- davinci-7b-compat (seq=256, batch=16): 620 tok/s, p50=30ms, p90=70ms, p99=180ms.

Quality/regression guardrails:
- We'll run the 200-query regression suite (attached) nightly during the pilot and surface any MRR/EM drops >4% as automatic alerts.
- Prompt hygiene: we suggest using prompt_set_search_v1.json as the canonical prompt pack for baseline comparisons.

Links and artifacts I've placed in the Drive folder: benchmark traces, p99 latency traces, node sizing doc, and the Redwood-verified profiles TSV (see related links).

I'll prepare a short SOW and a recommended PO template; Ben can share the HubSpot deal id to attach quotes.

—Marissa
